stop_rule.description: A topic stops when it has at least three review rounds and the last two produced no new valuable idea.

entries.title: MITRE ATT&CK techniques and tactics
entries.summary: Knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques used as the common language for what each rule detects.
entries.applicability: Every CyberGuard rule is mapped to its techniques and exported as a Navigator layer.
entries.risks: Technique IDs change between versions; the mapping states the version it targets.
entries.decision_reason: Needed to show coverage and gaps per technique.

entries.title: MITRE D3FEND defensive techniques
entries.summary: Knowledge graph of defensive countermeasures linked to offensive techniques.
entries.applicability: Each rule names its D3FEND detect and respond techniques.
entries.risks: Countermeasure names are still evolving.
entries.decision_reason: Gives the defensive action for each detection.

entries.title: MITRE ATLAS LLM prompt injection (AML.T0051)
entries.summary: Adversarial techniques against AI systems, including prompt injection through data the model reads.
entries.applicability: Evidence that instructs the AI analyst raises CG-AI-INJECTION-121 mapped to AML.T0051.
entries.risks: Pattern detection cannot prove the absence of injection; the structural controls carry the protection.
entries.decision_reason: Logs and mail are attacker-controlled text read by the analyst.

entries.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
entries.summary: Catalog of vulnerabilities with evidence of exploitation in the wild, with due dates for US federal agencies.
entries.applicability: KEV membership raises vulnerability priority and drives due dates.
entries.risks: US-centred; absence from KEV does not mean safe.
entries.decision_reason: Strongest public signal of real exploitation.

entries.title: NVD CVE API 2.0
entries.summary: Public API for CVE records with CPE applicability and CVSS metrics.
entries.applicability: Source of affected version ranges for software inventory matching.
entries.risks: Enrichment backlog and rate limits.
entries.decision_reason: Authoritative CVE data.

entries.title: FIRST EPSS exploit prediction scores
entries.summary: Daily probability that a CVE will be exploited in the next 30 days.
entries.applicability: Used next to KEV and exposure for risk ranking, not alone.
entries.risks: A probability, not proof of exploitation.
entries.decision_reason: Improves ranking beyond CVSS.

entries.title: Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) 1.3.0
entries.summary: Vendor-neutral event schema for security telemetry.
entries.applicability: Normalised logs are exported as OCSF classes with a per-format quality report.
entries.risks: Not every source field has an OCSF home; gaps are reported.
entries.decision_reason: Interoperability with SIEMs and data lakes.

entries.title: NCA Essential Cybersecurity Controls ECC-2:2024
entries.summary: 4 domains and 28 subdomains of baseline controls for government and CNI entities.
entries.applicability: Evidence mapping per subdomain with applicability by entity profile.
entries.risks: The Arabic text is binding; mapping is at subdomain level.
entries.decision_reason: Primary Saudi baseline for target customers.

entries.title: NCA Cloud Cybersecurity Controls CCC-2:2024
entries.summary: Extension of ECC for cloud providers (CSP) and tenants (CST): 4 domains, 24 subdomains.
entries.applicability: CST or CSP subdomain mapping when cloud is used or provided.
entries.risks: Control-level assessment uses the NCA tool.
entries.decision_reason: Applies to in-scope entities using cloud.

entries.title: NCA NPMSOC-1:2024 and RFMSOC-1:2024 (managed SOC policy and licensing)
entries.summary: Licensing is required to provide managed SOC services in the Kingdom, in two tiers, with residency and staffing obligations.
entries.applicability: Readiness gate before registering external customers.
entries.risks: Body text of the PDFs is drawn as images; non-heading points need confirmation against the Arabic text.
entries.decision_reason: Blocking condition before commercial service.

entries.title: NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 Guide to OT Security
entries.summary: Guidance for securing operational technology while keeping safety and availability first.
entries.applicability: Passive-first OT mode, no active scanning, separate safety approval.
entries.risks: Plant-specific procedures still decide.
entries.decision_reason: Prevents the platform from harming industrial processes.

entries.title: Falco runtime security
entries.summary: Kernel and container runtime detection engine emitting JSON alerts.
entries.applicability: Falco JSON alerts are parsed as IDS records.
entries.risks: Kernel driver or eBPF probe required on the host.
entries.decision_reason: Mature open source runtime signal for Linux and Kubernetes.

entries.title: Trivy image and SBOM scanning
entries.summary: Scanner for container images, file systems and SBOMs.
entries.applicability: Trivy JSON results feed container vulnerability alerts.
entries.risks: Database freshness determines results.
entries.decision_reason: Widely used, machine-readable output.

entries.title: SLSA provenance
entries.summary: Framework and provenance format describing how an artifact was built.
entries.applicability: Artifact verification checks provenance and trusted builders.
entries.risks: Provenance proves the build path, not the absence of malicious code.
entries.decision_reason: Standard way to verify build origin.

entries.title: YARA rules
entries.summary: Pattern-matching language for classifying files.
entries.applicability: Suspicious files are judged with YARA (or the built-in engine) without execution.
entries.risks: Rule quality decides false positives.
entries.decision_reason: Common format shared by threat intelligence teams.

entries.title: Windows LAPS
entries.summary: Rotation and backup of local administrator passwords to AD or Entra ID.
entries.applicability: LAPS posture is collected per host.
entries.risks: Legacy LAPS and Windows LAPS coexist in many estates.
entries.decision_reason: Shared local admin passwords enable lateral movement.

entries.title: CISA cybersecurity advisories used for incident studies
entries.summary: Published advisories describing real campaigns, techniques and mitigations.
entries.applicability: Eight cited incidents show which stages CyberGuard sees per installation.
entries.risks: Advisories describe past campaigns.
entries.decision_reason: Grounds detection priorities in documented attacks.

entries.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
entries.summary: Outcome-based framework with Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover functions.
entries.applicability: Security outcomes are reported by CSF function.
entries.risks: Outcomes, not controls; needs local profiles.
entries.decision_reason: Common executive language for posture.

entries.title: Batfish network configuration analysis
entries.summary: Builds a model from network configuration snapshots (vendor formats include Arista, F5 BIG-IP, Cisco NX-OS and IOS-XR, Dell Force10, Foundry, Juniper JunOS and Palo Alto) and answers reachability and differential questions before a change, through a Java service and the pybatfish Python client.
entries.applicability: Candidate external analyzer for vendors and features the native engine does not model; the native CG-131 engine covers normalised rulesets and IPv4 routes.
entries.risks: Separate Java service plus Python client (CyberGuard has no runtime dependencies); per-model feature coverage must be confirmed before results count in a decision.
entries.decision_reason: The native engine gives before/after reachability for stored snapshots now; Batfish is reconsidered when customers need multi-vendor control-plane simulation.

entries.title: Sigma generic detection rule format
entries.summary: Vendor-neutral YAML format for log detection rules with a large community rule set.
entries.applicability: Possible import format for detection-as-code hypotheses.
entries.risks: Rule licence terms and field mapping to CyberGuard records must be reviewed; community rules need tuning.
entries.decision_reason: Native declarative hypotheses (CG-065) cover current needs; revisit when importing community content.

entries.title: Native pre-change reachability engine
entries.summary: Evaluates required flows across firewall rulesets and IPv4 routes before and after a proposed change, marking unsupported rule features as unknown.
entries.applicability: Pre-change gate for ACL, firewall and route changes on devices with stored snapshots.
entries.risks: Does not model NAT, state, load balancers or asymmetric routing; results are configuration analysis only.
entries.decision_reason: Gives a safe, cannot-verify or unsafe decision with no new dependency.

entries.title: NIST SP 800-189 Rev. 1 BGP security and resilience
entries.summary: Initial public draft (comments closed February 25, 2025) recommending RPKI, ROAs, ROA-based route origin validation and prefix filtering for BGP, source address validation against spoofing, and RTBH and Flowspec for DDoS.
entries.applicability: Organisations that run BGP with their own AS or address space; not small LANs without BGP.
entries.risks: Still a draft, not a final publication: cite it as a draft and recheck its status before relying on it.
entries.decision_reason: Defines the checks CG-135 runs (ROV, ROA coverage, prefix filters); the final 2019 SP 800-189 remains the published reference.

entries.title: RFC 6811 BGP prefix origin validation and RFC 9319 maxLength guidance
entries.summary: Validation state of a route is valid, invalid or not-found against covering ROA payloads by origin AS and maxLength; RFC 9319 (BCP 185) advises against loose maxLength because it enables forged-origin sub-prefix hijacks.
entries.applicability: Route origin validation of routes in the router table and of the organisation prefixes.
entries.risks: Origin validation does not stop path manipulation with a forged origin AS.
entries.decision_reason: Implemented natively in lib/routing-security.js with no dependency.

entries.title: Routinator and rpki-client relying party software
entries.summary: Relying party software that fetches and validates the RPKI and exports validated ROA payloads as JSON (Routinator "vrps --format json"; rpki-client JSON output) and serves them to routers over RTR.
entries.applicability: Source of the validated ROA payloads imported by scripts/routing-security.js.
entries.risks: Running a validator is the operator's job; CyberGuard imports its export and does not validate the RPKI itself.
entries.decision_reason: The JSON export is imported now; embedding a validator or querying it live is reconsidered if customers need continuous validation.

entries.title: CISA/NSA/FBI Enhanced Visibility and Hardening Guidance for Communications Infrastructure
entries.summary: Joint guidance with Five Eyes partners: monitor configuration changes and administrative access, keep logs and flow telemetry off the device, restrict and harden management access, disable unused services and apply vendor-specific hardening for Cisco devices.
entries.applicability: Network devices the organisation owns, and carrier devices only with the carrier written authorization.
entries.risks: Written for communications providers; enterprise use takes the device hardening and visibility parts only.
entries.decision_reason: Hardening and visibility checks implemented on authorized configuration exports.

entries.title: CISA AA25-239A Countering Chinese State-Sponsored Actors (Salt Typhoon)
entries.summary: Names the exploited CVEs (Cisco Smart Install CVE-2018-0171, IOS XE web UI CVE-2023-20198 and CVE-2023-20273, PAN-OS CVE-2024-3400, Ivanti CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887) and techniques: ACL entries added for actor IPs, SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN mirroring, GRE/IPsec tunnels and static routes, Guest Shell containers, SSH on non-standard ports and IOS XR sshd_operns on TCP/57722; warns not to rely on device syslog alone.
entries.applicability: Detection of these configuration techniques between authorized exports.
entries.risks: Actors can change and restore configurations between exports; continuous AAA command accounting and off-box flows remain necessary.
entries.decision_reason: Technique checks implemented; exposure to the named CVEs is matched through the existing vulnerability catalogs.

entries.title: IOS XR sshd_operns host SSH on TCP/57722
entries.summary: An additional SSH endpoint to the IOS XR host Linux, disabled by default; enabling it gives shell access outside the IOS XR CLI.
entries.applicability: IOS XR routers.
entries.risks: The configuration line that enables it was not confirmed from a vendor document in this review; detecting TCP/57722 needs an authorized port observation.
entries.decision_reason: Added when an IOS XR configuration sample or port observation source is available.

entries.title: CISA ScubaGear (SCuBA Microsoft 365 assessment tool) 2.0.0
entries.summary: ScubaResults_{UUID}.json with MetaData (Tool, ToolVersion, TimestampZulu, ReportUUID), Summary and Results per product (AAD, SecuritySuite, EXO, PowerBI, PowerPlatform, SharePoint, Teams); controls MS.<PRODUCT>.<group>.<n>v<version> with Result and Criticality (Shall/Should, Not-Implemented, 3rd Party). Defender policies moved into the Security Suite in 2.0.0. Global Reader suffices for most products; Power Platform and the SharePoint app permission are write-capable.
entries.applicability: Import of the owner run as read-only evidence with policy versions and drift.
entries.risks: Not-Implemented and 3rd Party controls need manual evidence; Power Platform has no read-only role.
entries.decision_reason: Implemented as an import; CyberGuard never holds tenant credentials.

entries.title: CISA ScubaGoggles (SCuBA Google Workspace assessment tool) 1.1.0 and baselines
entries.summary: Same output schema as ScubaGear plus Result values No events found and Incorrect Result; Super Admin required; 9 of 11 OAuth scopes read-only (apps.licensing and apps.groups.settings are not); Common Controls, Gmail and Drive baselines assume Enterprise Plus; log-based checks miss settings never changed from default and reach back about six months.
entries.applicability: Import with a declared edition; log checks without events are unproven.
entries.risks: Super Admin is a high privilege for an assessment; the DLP edition list in the baseline is longer than what is encoded.
entries.decision_reason: Implemented with license-dependent and no-log-events states and a per-area comparison with Microsoft 365.

entries.title: Google Workspace Help: Context-Aware Access editions
entries.summary: Context-Aware Access is available in Frontline Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, Education Standard and Plus, Enterprise Essentials Plus and Cloud Identity Premium; users without a supported edition are not subject to its policies.
entries.applicability: Controls needing Context-Aware Access are license dependent on other editions.
entries.risks: Edition lists differ slightly between Google help pages; confirm in the Admin console.
entries.decision_reason: Encoded as the documented edition list for GWS.COMMONCONTROLS.2.

entries.title: AWS IAM Access Analyzer: analyzer types, ListFindingsV2 and pricing
entries.summary: Analyzer types ACCOUNT, ORGANIZATION, ACCOUNT_UNUSED_ACCESS, ORGANIZATION_UNUSED_ACCESS, ACCOUNT_INTERNAL_ACCESS, ORGANIZATION_INTERNAL_ACCESS set the zone of trust; status ACTIVE, CREATING, DISABLED, FAILED. ListFindingsV2 findingType ExternalAccess, UnusedIAMRole, UnusedIAMUserAccessKey, UnusedIAMUserPassword, UnusedPermission, InternalAccess; status ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, RESOLVED. External access has no additional charge and is regional; unused access is charged per IAM role or user analysed per month (one analyzer per partition); internal access is charged per resource monitored per region per month.
entries.applicability: Import of analyzers and findings with per-analysis state, region coverage and cost.
entries.risks: Pricing can change; the unused access age setting is read only through GetAnalyzer, which is not imported.
entries.decision_reason: Implemented; analyses that are not active are never read as no exposure.

entries.title: Microsoft Entra: Conditional Access for workload identities and workload identity risk
entries.summary: Policies apply only to single-tenant service principals registered in the tenant; Microsoft and third-party SaaS apps including multitenant apps are not covered and managed identities are not covered; policies assigned to a group are not enforced for service principals in it; Workload Identities Premium is required to create or modify them; block is the only grant. ID Protection workload identity detections exclude managed identities. Audit activities: Add service principal credentials, Update application - Certificates and secrets management, Consent to application, Add delegated permission grant, Add app role assignment to service principal, Add owner to application.
entries.applicability: Coverage classes and alerts for workload identities.
entries.risks: Service principal sign-ins are exposed through the beta signIns API and need Entra ID P1 or P2.
entries.decision_reason: Implemented; uncoverable identities are never shown as protected.

entries.title: CISA fact sheet: Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA
entries.summary: Ranks MFA from strongest to weakest: phishing-resistant (FIDO/WebAuthn and PKI-based), app-based OTP or push with number matching, push without number matching, SMS or voice as a last resort. Some systems may not support phishing-resistant MFA: start with services that do, phase rollout from administrators and help desk, and escalate systems without MFA to senior leadership.
entries.applicability: Tier ranking of registered methods and declared application exceptions.
entries.risks: Microsoft Entra methodsRegistered is a free-form collection; new values stay unclassified until mapped. Built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength allows Windows Hello for Business or platform credential, FIDO2 security key and multifactor certificate-based authentication.
entries.decision_reason: Implemented; registration is never read as enforcement.

entries.title: NIST SP 800-207A Zero Trust Architecture Model for Access Control in Cloud-Native Applications in Multi-Cloud Environments
entries.summary: Shifts access control from network parameters to application and service identities, with identity-tier and network-tier policies, service mesh and SPIFFE application identity infrastructure.
entries.applicability: Namespaces are classed by identity-tier versus network-tier authorization over effective mTLS.
entries.risks: Policies describe intent; actual traffic needs proxy access logs.
entries.decision_reason: Implemented for Istio exports and a declared inventory; not applicable without a mesh.

entries.title: SPIFFE concepts and SPIRE server defaults; Istio PeerAuthentication and AuthorizationPolicy
entries.summary: SPIFFE IDs spiffe://trust-domain/workload; keys short lived and rotated automatically; SPIRE default_x509_svid_ttl 1h and default_jwt_svid_ttl 5m. Istio mTLS UNSET without a parent is PERMISSIVE (plaintext or mTLS); an ALLOW AuthorizationPolicy with an empty spec allows nothing; source.principals requires mTLS.
entries.applicability: Effective mTLS, authorization tier and certificate lifetime checks.
entries.risks: No official Istio default workload certificate lifetime was confirmed, so the owner sets the limit.
entries.decision_reason: Implemented.

entries.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud: Defender CSPM attack path analysis, EASM integration and sensitive data
entries.summary: Attack path analysis and risk prioritization are in the paid Defender CSPM plan across Azure, AWS and GCP; external attack surface data validates internet exposure of entry points; data breach paths require sensitive data discovery.
entries.applicability: Comparison table and the validated versus inferred distinction.
entries.risks: Vendor graphs see more relationships (for example instance profiles) than imported records.
entries.decision_reason: Implemented from stored records with per-step evidence.
